tasks.prompt: Use case: compositing / precise-object-edit. Create a revised interior screenshot mockup of Ooga Booga Land's Timechain Sphere. IMAGE 1 is the EDIT TARGET, itself edited from a real gameplay screenshot: preserve its exact first-person camera, spherical room silhouette, simple low-poly procedural geometry, central meeting seating layout, human-sized chairs/table, tile sizes, workstation at left, closed double sliding exit doors at right, modest Exit button, actual game HUD/crop, flat game lighting and subtle scanlines. IMAGE 2 is the user's Timechain Index blocks dashboard screenshot, the precise source for the display styling and information architecture. Redesign ONLY the room's material palette, floor markings and display content to make it unmistakeably TIMECHAIN themed. Change navy/cyan surfaces to very dark charcoal/black with thin amber edge details and restrained golden light; keep ordinary game materials, NO glossy futuristic spaceship panels, neon ceiling ribs or holograms. Floor path is a subdued amber chain of connected rectangular block motifs leading to the same central meeting area; a small flat Bitcoin B inset on central table is enough. Above the wall screens put a continuous horizontal row of compact LATEST BLOCKS cards wrapping around the room: thin amber outlines, white block heights, green mining-pool names, small amber labels, like image 2. Rebuild main wall displays using image 2's black backgrounds, fine amber borders, small white values, amber section labels, green mining data. Six readable panel headings across wall: 'MEMPOOL & FEES', 'DIFFICULTY', 'LAST 144 BLOCKS', 'MINER DOMINANCE', 'BLOCK PRODUCTION', 'HASHRATE & DIFFICULTY'. Use the screenshot's compositions: mempool/difficulty donut gauges, small fee metric boxes, last144 summary cards and interval chips, ranked pool shares with a segmented color bar, production stats, and a real-looking jagged GREEN hashrate line over a thin AMBER stepped difficulty line on a dark grid. These must look like flat textured game screens, not floating GUIs. Reuse illustrative values only from image 2 where readable and otherwise tiny neutral strokes, do not invent new live facts. The two exit door leaves carry a continuation of the charcoal wall and amber block-chain strip across center seam; modest amber 'SPACE · EXIT' by button. Keep all content framed as concept visualization, not functioning live app: small bottom-left caption 'TIMECHAIN SPHERE · ROOMS 1–3 · 1×' and below 'SCREENSHOT MOCKUP · SAMPLE DATA'. Remove all obsolete Exploration/Resources/Building/Citizens/System headings and all cyan graphics. Preserve game's visual identity and exact viewpoint. Wide landscape matching original. The attached dashboard's styling must be clearly recognizable on the room walls.

Make a three-panel size comparison from this specific screenshot-edit mockup of Ooga Booga Land's Timechain Sphere. Three equal wide landscape panels stacked vertically. Preserve this exact black/charcoal low-poly spherical game interior, amber connected-block floor path, small normal-sized meeting chairs/table with Bitcoin mark, workstation, thin amber bordered Timechain Index dashboard walls, green and amber chart lines and latest-block cards wrapping above. No navy/cyan styling from older variants. Panel headings exactly 'ROOMS 1–3 · 1×', 'ROOMS 4–6 · 1.5×', 'ROOMS 7–9 · 2×'. Baseline first panel, then increase room architectural width, depth, height to 1.5x then2x. Same camera eye height/FOV in all panels, central normal-size furniture near foreground at same distance, increasingly distant outer walls and higher ceiling, more floor around same size furniture; do not simply zoom out or scale everything. Standard human-sized exit doors and button stay at right, physically farther away in large room; display layout scales with shell but label sizes stay readable. Use same chart designs each time, no invented new metrics; the charts are illustrative screenshot content. No original game HUD in this comparison sheet. Bottom caption 'SAME TIMECHAIN DESIGN · SEPARATE PRESENCE & VOICE PER ROOM' and smaller 'Architecture scales. Players, furniture and controls stay human-sized. Sample data.' Match source game's simple flat shaded rendering/scanlines; this should look like edits of the source screenshot, not new concept art.

Surgical screenshot edit: image1 is the exact edit target, an Ooga Booga Land door-open mockup from real gameplay screenshot. Image2 is the replacement interior reference. Keep everything outside image1's open doorway unchanged: huge orange Bitcoin sphere, ropes, timber bridge, opening and sign, camera/crop, game HUD, small keypad ROOM3 with only3 amber selected, colors lighting. ONLY replace the old navy/cyan room seen through the doorway with a correctly perspective-matched view into image2's Timechain themed black/charcoal interior: amber connected-block walkway aligned to the entrance, black normal-size chairs around low central Bitcoin table, thin amber outlines on black Timechain Index data screens, green/amber real-looking chart traces and latest-block card ribbon. No old 'Building/Citizens' headings. It should genuinely look through this doorway into the same revised room. Keep the two doors retracted sideways. Preserve the source game screenshot style and all exterior geometry.

Surgical layout correction to this screenshot-based Timechain Sphere mockup. Keep the exact black/charcoal low-poly Ooga Booga Land game style, first-person eye height, spherical room, game HUD, amber block-chain floor path, meeting table/chairs, all six Timechain Index panel designs and top latest-block cards. The entrance and exit are the SAME doorway, centered BEHIND THIS CAMERA, on the axis opposite the middle of the screens. Correct only the room layout in every panel of this three-size screenshot comparison. Preserve all three labels ROOMS1–3 1x, ROOMS4–6 1.5x, ROOMS7–9 2x, progressively larger room architecture, normal furniture/player scale, black-charcoal game materials, amber chain floor paths, six Timechain Index chart panels, green/amber data graphics and latest-block ribbon. Keep each panel's full room and all dimensional differences, labels and footer legible. Preserve the exact screenshot-derived Ooga Booga Land rendering style. Minor footer addition 'Entry and exit centered behind viewer'. Do not redesign charts or invent a second entrance.

Create the REVERSE first-person screenshot mockup of this exact Ooga Booga Land Timechain room, turning 180 degrees to face back toward its entrance/exit. Match this screenshot's black-charcoal low-poly procedural game geometry, dark tiled floor, restrained amber lighting, original Ooga HUD and modest scanlines. The entrance/exit is ONE standard human-sized pair of closed sliding doors precisely CENTERED in the rear curved wall and aligned with the room's center and amber chain-pattern walkway. A narrow vertical center seam, left/right leaves continue adjacent charcoal-and-amber wall stripe/connected-block motif across seam. The six major chart screens are on the opposite FRONT hemisphere BEHIND THE VIEWER and should NOT appear behind or above this rear door; at most a sliver of the distant display wall at the extreme left/right edges. Clear uncluttered passage to this centered door. Let backs of a couple small meeting chairs/edge of table appear at lower margins to establish same room, without blocking centered door/path. Do not enlarge door to monumental size or add extra portals, sci-fi machinery or new lighting. This is a concept edit consistent with actual game screenshot, not photorealism. Bottom-left caption 'REVERSE VIEW · CENTERED EXIT OPPOSITE SCREENS'. This reverse view proves the entrance/exit is directly opposite and centered on the data wall's axis.
